question: Something went wrong with this Tamoz runtime in the last few hours. Use the probes to investigate its own record and report the root cause. Set the hypothesis field to exactly one error code identifying the root cause, with no other words or punctuation. Discuss your reasoning and other codes in the findings.

error.message: 402 Payment Required: the account balance is empty

findings.statement: Root cause: four model.generate.plan effects on thread.noise.5 failed with Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError code 'insufficient_balance' within 11 ms (1791142681250-1791142681261), the only repeating failure class+code in the window. Both fired rules (effect.repeated_failure, model.call_failed, both high severity, category dependency_unavailable) point at it, and the model.call_failed rule states that an empty account is a provider problem, not a Tamoz bug.

The failures did not block traffic: all 6 turns requested in the window completed (thread.noise.0 through .5), 30 of 35 effects succeeded, the runtime reports degraded=false with zero occurrences and an empty journal. The five failures are one isolated burst on one thread, not a service-wide outage.

The error code 'not_found' (Tamoz::Agent::ToolError on one tool.read_file at 1791142681264, thread.noise.5) is noise, not the root cause: it occurred once, fired no rule, and a missing file is a request-level condition, whereas the recurring-failure rule singled out ModelCallError/insufficient_balance. No other error codes appear anywhere in the record for either window.

Each failing effect was single-shot (attempt 1, no retries) and idempotent, yet four distinct effect keys failed with the identical code in sequence, consistent with a worker draining tasks after the provider balance ran out; effect.repeated_failure's action says to fix that one cause instead of retrying the calls.

proposals.action: Top up or repair the model provider account (billing/balance), then re-run probe_self_diagnose and confirm no new ModelCallError/insufficient_balance attempts appear.
proposals.rationale: Both high-severity rules point to a single recurring provider refusal; fixing the account once clears the cause of all four failures.

proposals.action: Do not retry the four failed model.generate.plan effects until the balance is fixed; rely on their idempotent effect keys instead.
proposals.rationale: The effect.repeated_failure rule's own action is to fix the one recurring cause instead of retrying the calls.

proposals.action: Ignore the single tool.read_file not_found unless it repeats for the same path.
proposals.rationale: One occurrence, no matching rule, different failure class; treating it as the incident would misdirect the fix.

findings.statement: In the 240-minute window the runtime recorded 38 effect attempts with 8 failures and 30 successes, and 6 completed turns; the summary shows no other failure counts and degraded=false.

All 8 failures are model.converse.work_step attempts on thread.noise.5, each Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError with code rate_limited, each failing on attempt 1 with no retry, between at_ms 1791142681251 and 1791142681278 (~27 ms).

In the same window exactly 6 write_file approvals were asked and all 6 were approved; the failures immediately follow the burst of approvals, consistent with a burst of parallel model calls tripping a rate limit.

Thread.noise.5's own execution completed: 3 model.generate.plan and 2 tool.read_file effects succeeded before the 8 rate_limited work_step failures, so earlier steps were healthy and only the high-volume model call step failed.
No other error class or code appears anywhere in the window: the only failure kind is model.converse.work_step / rate_limited, and no worker errors are logged.
Threads noise.0 through noise.4 completed normally around the same time, so the problem is not workspace-wide or environmental in general — it is tied to the burst of concurrent converse calls.

gaps.why: The runtime record shows single-attempt failures with no backoff, but not what limit or retry configuration is in place, so I cannot say whether the limit was misconfigured or simply exceeded.

proposals.action: Add retry with exponential backoff (honoring retry-after) for rate_limited failures on model.converse.work_step effects.
proposals.rationale: Each rate_limited failure ended on attempt 1 with no retry, turning a transient throttle into a permanent effect failure.

proposals.action: Cap or queue the concurrency of parallel model.converse.work_step calls per thread/execution.
proposals.rationale: All 8 failures landed within ~27 ms of a burst of approvals, so the failures look like a self-inflicted concurrency burst rather than sustained overload.

findings.statement: Every failed effect in the 24h window is tool.read_file failing with Tamoz::Agent::ToolError code path_outside_workspace. 12 of 12 failures, all on thread.noise.5, each on its first attempt (attempt_number 1, no retries); the other 30 effects succeeded.

The burst is tightly clustered: 1791142825899–1791142825926 (~27 ms), each attempt failing in ≤1 ms. That profile means the workspace path guard rejected the requested path immediately — not a timeout, not a missing file, not a dependency outage.

Within the same execution 88a7fba2 on thread.noise.5, two tool.read_file effects succeeded before the 12 failures, and 18 model.generate.plan calls succeeded across threads. Consistent with the turn reading valid workspace-relative paths, then repeatedly requesting paths that resolve outside the workspace root.

The rule engine's only finding is effect.repeated_failure (severity high, category dependency_unavailable, count 12), citing exactly those 12 attempts; occurrences table is otherwise empty and degraded=false with no degraded_reasons.

Everything else in the window is healthy: 6/6 turns requested and completed (threads noise.0–noise.5), all 6 write_file approvals asked and approved, no failed-unknown or unknown effect states, no logged worker errors, journal 0 documents/0 drops. A 240-minute and a 1440-minute lookback return identical events, so nothing older contributes.

Interpretive caveat: all six threads carry synthetic 'noise' naming, so the burst could be injected fixture traffic rather than organic agent behavior. Even so, it is the only failure signature in the runtime's own record and the only rule that fired, so it is the incident by the record's own account.

gaps.datum: The requested path argument for each failed read_file
gaps.why: The probe record exposes only error class and code, not the effect parameters, so I cannot tell whether one bad path prefix (e.g., an absolute /tmp or /private/var path) caused all 12, or whether the turn looped over many external paths. That distinguishes a single config/prompt mistake from a model loop.

gaps.datum: runtime.sqlite3 raw rows
gaps.why: The probes cite runtime.sqlite3 as the source, but the workspace directory is empty (list_directory returned nothing), so I could not inspect row-level detail such as params or retry policy beyond what the probes returned.

gaps.datum: Worker-side stack traces
gaps.why: No worker errors were logged in the window (timeline shows none), so there is no caller context for the failed reads beyond the effect_attempt rows.

proposals.action: Reject out-of-workspace paths at planning/validation time instead of at effect execution
proposals.rationale: All 12 failures were immediate guard rejections; surfacing the same code to the model before the effect is queued would stop the loop earlier. Match the rule's own advice: fix the one cause, don't retry the calls.

proposals.action: Alert on the first path_outside_workspace per thread rather than after 12 repeats
proposals.rationale: effect.repeated_failure only fired after the burst was already complete (~27 ms, 12 failures); a first-occurrence rule would shorten time-to-signal for a fast repeating failure.

proposals.action: Record the offending path argument (redacted) on path_outside_workspace attempts
proposals.rationale: The probes carry class and code only; capturing the requested path would let an operator tell a bad configured root from model misbehavior without raw database access.

findings.statement: Scope of the incident: in the 4-hour window (and identically over 24h) the runtime itself was healthy — degraded=false, all 6 turns completed, 30 of 36 effects succeeded, all 12 tool.read_file calls passed, occurrences=0 (no logged worker errors), truncated=false. Every failure is a model call made inside one turn, thread.noise.5.

The dominant, repeating failure: 5 of the 6 failed effects are model.generate.plan calls in thread.noise.5, every one Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError with code authentication_failed, each dying on attempt 1 in 0-1ms — an immediate rejection, no timeout, no partial response, no later retry succeeding. The built-in rule effect.repeated_failure fires on exactly this code, category dependency_unavailable, with the guidance to fix that cause once instead of retrying.

Timing localizes the cause: within the same turn, three model.generate.plan effects succeeded at ms ...9941, ...9943 and ...9946, then from ms ...9956 onward every plan effect was refused with authentication_failed. The provider accepted the credential and then stopped accepting it mid-turn — consistent with a revoked/expired key or an emptied account, not a code change and not a Tamoz bug (the runtime's own action text: a refused key or empty account is a provider problem).

The other code in the window, rate_limited, appears exactly once (model.generate.review at ms ...9970, same thread) and is a downstream symptom, not the root cause: a throttle cannot produce authentication rejections, it followed the 5 auth failures rather than preceding them, and it cost nothing — the turn still completed. It should be retried, not investigated as the cause.

Ruled out: no other error class or code appears anywhere — the 1440-minute diagnose returns the same rules digest (sha256:db8a96fb...) and identical row counts as the 240-minute run, so nothing earlier is hidden; no journal drops or occurrences; every request ended 'completed'; the write_file approval ask/approve cycle worked on all six turns including the affected one, so policy/approval machinery is not implicated.

gaps.datum: Provider-side response bodies / HTTP status detail for the five authentication_failed calls.
gaps.why: The record stores only class and code, so revoked key vs expired key vs empty/overdue account cannot be distinguished; the provider console or key vault has to answer that.

gaps.datum: Which credential or profile thread.noise.5 used and what changed around ms 1791143019950.
gaps.why: Authentication succeeded at ...9946 and was refused at ...9956; knowing what changed in that gap (rotation, revocation, quota exhaustion) would confirm the trigger.

gaps.datum: Whether the rate_limited review call was ever retried successfully after ms ...9970.
gaps.why: Only one attempt is recorded and the turn still completed, but the record alone cannot show a later review elsewhere.

proposals.action: Verify and rotate the model provider API key for the profile used by thread.noise.5, then re-run one model.generate.plan to confirm acceptance.
proposals.rationale: Five immediate authentication_failed rejections with successes in the same seconds before them indicate the credential stopped being valid; the fix is provider-side, not in Tamoz code.

proposals.action: Fail fast on authentication_failed: stop retrying and stop fanning out further model calls, alert, and require operator intervention.
proposals.rationale: The turn burned five plan attempts in 12ms against a dead credential; the effect.repeated_failure rule itself recommends fixing the single cause instead of retrying.

proposals.rationale: The one rate_limited occurrence lost a review with no recorded retry; throttling is transient and normally self-heals.

proposals.action: Alert on the first authentication_failed occurrence per window rather than only on repeated failures.
proposals.rationale: The condition is non-transient, so the first occurrence is already actionable; waiting for a count of 5 delays the fix.

Summary: You asked what went wrong with this Tamoz runtime in the last few hours. The probes (diagnose and timeline over 240 and 1440 minutes, plus the turn record for thread.noise.5) show the runtime itself was healthy: all 6 turns completed, 30 of 36 effects succeeded, and every failure is a model call inside a single turn — 5 model.generate.plan calls rejected with Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError/authentication_failed and one model.generate.review with code rate_limited. The repeating, non-transient code that explains the incident is authentication_failed: plan calls succeeded through ms 1791143019946 in that turn and were refused from ms ...9956 onward, so the provider credential stopped being accepted mid-turn.
Hypothesis (high confidence): authentication_failed
Findings:
1. Scope of the incident: in the 4-hour window (and identically over 24h) the runtime itself was healthy — degraded=false, all 6 turns completed, 30 of 36 effects succeeded, all 12 tool.read_file calls passed, occurrences=0 (no logged worker errors), truncated=false. Every failure is a model call made inside one turn, thread.noise.5. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_timeline]
2. The dominant, repeating failure: 5 of the 6 failed effects are model.generate.plan calls in thread.noise.5, every one Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError with code authentication_failed, each dying on attempt 1 in 0-1ms — an immediate rejection, no timeout, no partial response, no later retry succeeding. The built-in rule effect.repeated_failure fires on exactly this code, category dependency_unavailable, with the guidance to fix that cause once instead of retrying. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_explain_turn]
3. Timing localizes the cause: within the same turn, three model.generate.plan effects succeeded at ms ...9941, ...9943 and ...9946, then from ms ...9956 onward every plan effect was refused with authentication_failed. The provider accepted the credential and then stopped accepting it mid-turn — consistent with a revoked/expired key or an emptied account, not a code change and not a Tamoz bug (the runtime's own action text: a refused key or empty account is a provider problem). [from probe_self_explain_turn]
4. The other code in the window, rate_limited, appears exactly once (model.generate.review at ms ...9970, same thread) and is a downstream symptom, not the root cause: a throttle cannot produce authentication rejections, it followed the 5 auth failures rather than preceding them, and it cost nothing — the turn still completed. It should be retried, not investigated as the cause. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_timeline]
5. Ruled out: no other error class or code appears anywhere — the 1440-minute diagnose returns the same rules digest (sha256:db8a96fb...) and identical row counts as the 240-minute run, so nothing earlier is hidden; no journal drops or occurrences; every request ended 'completed'; the write_file approval ask/approve cycle worked on all six turns including the affected one, so policy/approval machinery is not implicated. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_timeline]
Still unknown:
- Provider-side response bodies / HTTP status detail for the five authentication_failed calls.: The record stores only class and code, so revoked key vs expired key vs empty/overdue account cannot be distinguished; the provider console or key vault has to answer that.
- Which credential or profile thread.noise.5 used and what changed around ms 1791143019950.: Authentication succeeded at ...9946 and was refused at ...9956; knowing what changed in that gap (rotation, revocation, quota exhaustion) would confirm the trigger.
- Whether the rate_limited review call was ever retried successfully after ms ...9970.: Only one attempt is recorded and the turn still completed, but the record alone cannot show a later review elsewhere.
Proposed next actions (not executed; ask for one to run it through approval):
1. Verify and rotate the model provider API key for the profile used by thread.noise.5, then re-run one model.generate.plan to confirm acceptance.: Five immediate authentication_failed rejections with successes in the same seconds before them indicate the credential stopped being valid; the fix is provider-side, not in Tamoz code. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_explain_turn]
2. Fail fast on authentication_failed: stop retrying and stop fanning out further model calls, alert, and require operator intervention.: The turn burned five plan attempts in 12ms against a dead credential; the effect.repeated_failure rule itself recommends fixing the single cause instead of retrying. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_timeline]
3. Add backoff-and-retry for rate_limited on model.generate.review.: The one rate_limited occurrence lost a review with no recorded retry; throttling is transient and normally self-heals. [from probe_self_diagnose]
4. Alert on the first authentication_failed occurrence per window rather than only on repeated failures.: The condition is non-transient, so the first occurrence is already actionable; waiting for a count of 5 delays the fix. [from probe_self_timeline, probe_self_diagnose]
